contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A huge medieval manuscript famous for its full-page image of the devil.
The Codex Gigas contains biblical, historical, medical, and penitential texts. Its size and imagery made it one of the most memorable manuscripts of medieval central Europe.

contentSections.title: Description
paragraphs: Codex Gigas is a material or textual object whose physical survival helps historians read medieval politics, belief, art, or memory.

contentSections.title: Origin and dating
paragraphs: The archive date of 1229 is an orientation point. Exact dating, patronage, or production context may be debated depending on the object.

contentSections.title: Historical context
paragraphs: Codex Gigas belongs to the world of Bohemia, where objects, texts, relics, and images could carry authority across generations.

contentSections.title: Use or meaning
paragraphs: The Codex Gigas functioned as an enormous monastic compendium, bringing together biblical text, historical writing, medical material, calendars, and penitential material in a single spectacular volume. Its size and famous devil image made it memorable, but its real importance lies in the range of knowledge preserved by one Benedictine manuscript.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Codex Gigas remains a useful witness because it gives material form to medieval culture rather than reducing history to rulers and battles.
